## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** No issue found in the tested scope. The change leaves a DSP filter chain's own capture stream in place when the audio input is switched, while application recording streams still move to the selected source.

The comparison below comes from a private PipeWire 1.6.8 / WirePlumber 0.5.17 / pipewire-pulse test setup. It used a synthetic filter chain whose capture stream has the same properties as asahi-audio's J413 microphone chain (`target.object` set, `node.dont-fallback = true`, no `node.linger`, no `application.name`):

| Scenario (synthetic chain) | Current helper | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Select the chain's own output source | Chain capture destroyed; chain and its output source removed | Chain stays linked to its configured source |
| Select an unrelated source | Chain capture destroyed; chain and its output source removed | Chain stays linked to its configured source |
| Pulse client and `pw-record` streams | Moved | Moved |
| Unnamed `pw-loopback` capture without a target | Moved by the helper | Not moved by the helper; WirePlumber relinked it to the new default |

The awk selection is identical to the one `bin/omarchy-audio-output-set-default` already uses, and the audio panel caller is unchanged.

**Suggested change (code comment):** The new comment attributes the teardown to pointing the chain's input at its own output. With the current helper, the synthetic chain was also destroyed when an unrelated microphone was selected. Source review of pipewire-pulse, WirePlumber 0.5.17 and module-filter-chain explains why:

```text
set-default-source X
  -> move-source-output <chain capture> X      (X is already the default)
  -> pipewire-pulse stores target.object = -1  ("follow the default")
  -> WirePlumber find-defined-target.lua: node.dont-fallback, no usable target -> destroy node
  -> module-filter-chain: capture stream unconnected -> whole module unloads (capture + output)
  -> WirePlumber software-dsp recreates the chain only when its parent device node is added again
```

Describing the trigger as any move of a `node.dont-fallback` DSP capture stream would keep a later edit from narrowing the guard to the self-target case only.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Private PipeWire 1.6.8, WirePlumber 0.5.17 and pipewire-pulse (pactl 17.0) setup with a synthetic `builtin copy` filter chain hosted in a separate PipeWire process, not asahi-audio's WirePlumber-loaded beamformer. Not tested on Apple Silicon hardware. Source review covered PipeWire 1.4.8 and 1.6.9, WirePlumber 0.5.17, asahi-audio, PulseAudio 17.0 `pactl` and Arch packaging. The author's hardware result and test runs were not reproduced.
